next.name: GOLD LOTUS
next.headline: GOLD LOTUS: the BlackByte ransomware operation, and what reports say about its Conti links
next.in_short: GOLD LOTUS is the Secureworks name for the group behind BlackByte ransomware. Two vendors say it grew out of the Conti ransomware scene. A 2023 report describes a new version of its malware.

sentences.t: GOLD LOTUS is a threat group tracked by Secureworks. The catalogue lists BlackByte and Hecamede as its other names.
Deep Instinct says that after Conti broke up, former leaders and affiliates set up under new names, and it lists BlackByte among them.
Intel 471 says other reports indicate that some ransomware-as-a-service operations, including BlackByte, have employed former Conti operators.
The catalogue lists these tools for the group: BlackByte, ExByte, Cobalt Strike, MEGA, RDP and SoftPerfect Network Scanner.
A November 2021 overview describes BlackByte as then recently discovered ransomware. Its core payload is a .NET DLL.
The same overview says BlackByte, unlike most ransomware today, uses a single symmetric encryption key. It adds that, like most ransomware, it can spread on its own to other machines.
A Picus Security report on May 2023 says the BlackByte ransomware gang launched a new version of its ransomware, called BlackByte NT.
Defenders should limit and monitor remote desktop access, watch for unexpected network scanning tools, and keep offline backups.
